title: The twisted convolution identity and ghost $r$-SICs from finite quantum dilogarithms
authors: Marcus Appleby, Steven T. Flammia, Gene S. Kopp
abstract: Radchenko and Wheeler (RW) recently proved a finite pentagon relation for real quadratic special values of the modular quantum dilogarithm and used it to establish the rank-$1$ twisted convolution identity conjectured by the current authors. RW gave an explicit argument in the principal case and remarked that their proof holds for all rank-$1$ admissible tuples. We extend their proof to all rank-$r$ admissible tuples and provide an explicit dictionary between the modular quantum dilogarithm and the Shintani-Faddeev modular cocycle conventions in the respective papers. Thus, we establish that, if $d,r$ are positive integers such that $r<\frac{d-1}{2}$ and $\frac{d^2-1}{r(d-r)} \in \mathbb{Z}$, then there exist ghost $r$-SICs: i.e., configurations of $d^2$ rank-$r$ subspaces in $\mathbb{C}^d$ that satisfy a non-Hermitian equichordal condition. Under the Stark conjecture, these configurations are Galois conjugate to Hermitian equichordal configurations called $r$-SICs (or rank-$r$ SIC-POVMs).
summary: This theoretical paper proves a generalized twisted convolution identity and establishes the existence of 'ghost r-SICs' using advanced techniques involving the modular quantum dilogarithm. It connects abstract algebraic identities derived from modular forms to concrete structures in quantum information theory, particularly concerning optimal quantum measurements.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish the twisted convolution identity (TCI) and prove the existence of 'ghost r-SICs' (configurations of subspaces satisfying a non-Hermitian equichordal condition).
main_result: The authors establish the TCI for specific parameters and prove the existence of ghost r-SICs for any admissible tuple, with genuine r-SICs being conditional on the Stark conjectures.
method: The proof extends a known pentagon relation from rank-1 to general rank-r tuples, utilizing character theory and explicit dictionaries between modular quantum dilogarithm conventions.
model_or_system: The theory is rooted in the modular quantum dilogarithm and its relation to the Shintani-Faddeev modular cocycle. The physical manifestation involves configurations of rank-r subspaces in $\mathbb{C}^d$, relevant to quantum information theory (SIC-POVMs).
key_observables: The existence of ghost r-SICs ($\tilde{\Pi}_p$), the twisted convolution identity (Equation 7), and the modular quantum dilogarithm values.
important_parameters: Admissible tuples $(d, r, Q)$ satisfying $r < \frac{d-1}{2}$ and $\frac{d^2-1}{r(d-r)} \in \mathbb{Z}$.
main_assumptions: The derivation of genuine r-SICs from ghost r-SICs relies on the unproven Stark conjectures regarding the action of the Galois group.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first establishing relationships between the quantum dilogarithm and the modular cocycle (Prop 2.1), proving a pentagon relation for subgroups (Thm 3.1), and finally deriving the TCI (Thm 1.2) which leads to the existence proof for ghost r-SICs (Thm 1.3).
why_interesting: The deep connection between number theory (modular forms, dilogarithms) and quantum information structures (SIC-POVMs) suggests underlying mathematical symmetries governing quantum measurement theory.
